title: Schwarzschild radius grows in proportion to mass
caption: r_s = 2GM/c² is about 2.95 km for each solar mass, so a 10 M☉ black hole has r_s ≈ 29.5 km: a horizon the size of a city.
alt: Schwarzschild radius in kilometres against mass in solar masses, a straight line through the origin reaching 29.5 kilometres at 10 solar masses.
description: Doubling the mass doubles the radius, so the mean density inside falls as 1/M²: supermassive black holes are less dense than water.

checks.name: 2GM☉/c² = 2.95 km (powers of ten cancel to km)
